<h>Lectio 1</h>
De libro primo Regum
<r>1 Reg 5:1-5</r>
<n>1</n> Philísthiim autem tulérunt arcam Dei et asportavérunt eam a Lápide adiutórii in Azótum.
<n>2</n> Tulerúntque Philísthiim arcam Dei et intulérunt eam in templum Dagon et statuérunt eam iuxta Dagon.
<n>3</n> Cumque surrexíssent dilúculo Azótii áltera die, ecce Dagon iacébat pronus in terra ante arcam Dómini; et tulérunt Dagon et restituérunt eum in locum suum.
<n>4</n> Rursúmque mane die áltera consurgéntes invenérunt Dagon iacéntem super fáciem suam in terra coram arca Dómini; caput autem Dagon et duæ palmæ mánuum eius abscíssæ erant super limen;
<n>5</n> Porro Dagon solus truncus remánserat in loco suo.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Audi, Dómine, hymnum et oratiónem, quam servus tuus orat coram te hódie, ut sint óculi tui apérti, et aures tuæ inténtæ,
* Super domum istam die ac nocte.
<r>℣.</r> Réspice, Dómine, de sanctuário tuo, et de excélso cælórum habitáculo.
<r>℟.</r> Super domum istam die ac nocte.

<h>Reading 1</h>
Lesson from the first book of Samuel
<r>1 Sam 5:1-5</r>
<n>1</n> And the Philistines took the ark of God, and carried it from the Stone of help into Azotus.
<n>2</n> And the Philistines took the ark of God, and brought it into the temple of Dagon, and set it by Dagon.
<n>3</n> And when the Azotians arose early the next day, behold Dagon lay upon his face on the ground before the ark of the Lord: and they took Dagon, and set him again in his place.
<n>4</n> And the next day again, when they rose in the morning, they found Dagon lying upon his face on the earth before the ark of the Lord: and the head of Dagon, and both the palms of his hands were cut off upon the threshold:
<n>5</n> And only the stump of Dagon remained in its place.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> Hearken, O Lord, unto the cry and to the prayer which thy servant prayeth before thee today, that thine eyes may be open and thine ears attend;
* Toward this house day and night.
<r>℣.</r> Look down from thine high and holy place, O Lord, even from heaven thy dwelling.
<r>℟.</r> Toward this house, day and night.

<r>1 Reg 5:6-8</r>
<n>6</n> Aggraváta est autem manus Dómini super Azótios, et demolítus est eos. Et ebulliérunt villæ et agri in médio regiónis illíus, et nati sunt mures, et facta est confúsio mortis magnæ in civitáte.
<n>7</n> Vidéntes autem viri Azótii huiuscémodi plagam dixérunt: Non máneat arca Dei Israël apud nos, quóniam dura est manus eius super nos et super Dagon deum nostrum.
<n>8</n> Et mitténtes congregavérunt omnes sátrapas Philisthinórum ad se et dixérunt: Quid faciémus de arca Dei Israël? Responderúntque Gethǽi: Circumducátur arca Dei Israël.

<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Peccávi super númerum arénæ maris, et multiplicáta sunt peccáta mea: et non sum dignus vidére altitúdinem cæli præ multitúdine iniquitátis meæ: quóniam irritávi iram tuam,
* Et malum coram te feci.
<r>℣.</r> Quóniam iniquitátem meam ego cognósco: et delíctum meum contra me est semper, quia tibi soli peccávi.
<r>℟.</r> Et malum coram te feci.

<h>Reading 2</h>
<r>1 Sam 5:6-8</r>
<n>6</n> And the hand of the Lord was heavy upon the Azotians, and he destroyed them, and afflicted Azotus and the coasts thereof with emerods. b.981cf689e1:
<h>Oratio</h>
<c>K</c>ýrie, eléison. Christe, eléison. Kýrie, eléison.
<n><k>Pater Noster</k> dicitur secreto usque ad <k>Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:</k></n>
<c>P</c>ater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris:
<r>℣.</r> Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
<r>℟.</r> Sed líbera nos a malo.

<r>℣.</r> Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
<r>℟.</r> Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>S</c>ancti nóminis tui, Dómine, timórem páriter et amórem fac nos habére perpétuum: quia nunquam tua gubernatióne destítuis, quos in soliditáte tuæ dilectiónis instítuis.
<h>P</h>er Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
b.740022ab21:
<h>Prayer</h>
<c>L</c>ord have mercy upon us, Christ have mercy upon us, Lord have mercy upon us.
<n><k>Our Father</k> is said silently until <k>And lead us not into temptation:</k>.</n>
<c>O</c>ur Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.
<r>℣.</r> And lead us not into temptation:
<r>℟.</r> But deliver us from evil.

<r>℣.</r> O Lord, hear my prayer.
<r>℟.</r> And let my cry come unto thee.
<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>O</c> Lord, Who never failest to help and govern them whom Thou dost bring up in thy steadfast fear and love keep us, we beseech thee, under the protection of thy good providence, and make us to have a perpetual fear and love of thy Holy Name.
<h>T</h>hrough Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

b.7148dd228b:
<h>Martyrologium</h>
<c>T</c>értio Nonas Iúnii Luna vicésima octáva. Anno Dómini 2027
<h>O</h>ctáva sanctíssimi Córporis Christi.
<h>A</h>rétii, in Túscia, sanctórum Mártyrum Pergentíni et Laurentíni fratrum, qui, in persecutióne Décii, sub Tibúrtio Prǽside, cum essent púeri, ibídem, post dira supplícia toleráta et magna mirácula osténsa, gládio cæsi sunt.
<h>C</h>onstantinópoli sanctórum Mártyrum Lucilliáni et quátuor puerórum, scílicet Cláudii, Hypátii, Pauli et Dionýsii. His cum púeris Lucilliánus, ex idolórum sacerdóte Christiánus factus, in fornácem, post vária torménta, iniéctus est, sed, flamma imbre exstíncta, omnes illǽsi evasérunt; dénique, ipse cruci affíxus, púeri autem gládio obtruncáti, sub Silváno Prǽside, consummáti sunt.
<h>C</h>órdubæ, in Hispánia, beáti Isaac Mónachi, qui, pro Christi fide, gládio necátus est.
<h>C</h>onstantinópoli sanctæ Paulæ, Vírginis et Mártyris, quæ, cum prædictórum Mártyrum Lucilliáni ac Sociórum sánguinem collígeret, ídeo, comprehénsa, virgis percússa, et in ignem coniécta sed liberáta, demum et ipsa eódem loco, ubi sanctus Lucilliánus crucifíxus fúerat, decolláta est.
<h>C</h>arthágine sancti Cæcílii Presbýteri, qui sanctum Cypriánum ad Christi fidem perdúxit.
<h>I</h>n território Aurelianénsi sancti Liphárdi, Presbýteri et Confessóris.
<h>L</h>ucæ, in Túscia, sancti Davíni Confessóris.
<h>A</h>nániæ sanctæ Olívæ Vírginis.
<h>L</h>utétiæ Parisiórum sanctæ Clotíldis Regínæ, cuius précibus vir eius Clodovéus, Rex Francórum, Christi fidem suscépit.
<r>℣.</r> Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
b.5f59db3b46:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>J</c>une 3rd 2027, the 28th day of the Moon, were born into the better life:
<h>T</h>he Octave of the most Sacred Body of Christ.
<h>A</h>t Arezzo, in Tuscany, the holy brethren Pergentinus and Laurentinus, both martyrs. They were boys, who, in the persecution under Decius, after bearing horrid torments and showing forth great works of power, were slain by the sword under the President Tiburtius.
<h>A</h>t Constantinople, the holy martyr Lucillian and his four sons, Claud, Hypatius, Paul, and Denis. Lucillian, before he became a Christian, had been a priest of idols. All the five, after they had been put to various tortures, were cast into a furnace, but rain put out the fire, and they all escaped unhurt. Then Lucillian was crucified, and the children were beheaded, and so under Silvanus the President they finished their testimony.
<h>A</h>t Cordova, in Spain, the blessed monk Isaac, who, [in the year 851,] was slain with the sword, [by the Muslims,] for Christ's faith's sake.
<h>A</h>t Constantinople, the holy Virgin and martyr Paula, who was arrested while she was gathering up the blood of the aforesaid martyrs Lucillian and his companions. She was beaten with rods, and cast into the fire, but was delivered, and at last beheaded at the same place where the holy Lucillian had been crucified.
<h>A</h>t Carthage, the holy Priest Caecilius, who brought holy Cyprian to believe in Christ.
<h>I</h>n the country of Orleans, [in the year 565,] the holy Confessor Liphard the Priest.
<h>A</h>t Lucca, in Tuscany, [in the year 1051,] the holy Confessor Davin, [the Armenian pilgrim.]
<h>A</h>t Anagni, the holy Virgin Oliva.
<h>A</h>t Paris, the holy Queen Clotilde, at whose entreaties her husband, King Clovis, accepted the faith of Christ.
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.
